On success the old s->session is freed (4552) and new_sess is stored into s->session (4553), transferring ownership to the connection object, which frees it during its normal teardown. The allocation is therefore not leaked; it is an intentional ownership transfer, not a NeverFree.

The malloc at line 3181 is stored in the persistent struct member s->pha_context, not a local variable. Ownership is transferred to the SSL_CONNECTION object. The same buffer is freed before reallocation (OPENSSL_free at line 3179) and managed across the connection lifecycle, so it is not leaked within this function. On allocation failure the code sets pha_context_len=0 and returns an error, which is correct handling.

The allocation at line 1680 is stored in the persistent struct field s->ext.ech.innerch, not a local variable. Ownership is transferred to the SSL session structure. Line 1673 (OPENSSL_free(s->ext.ech.innerch)) in the same slice shows this field is freed before reassignment, confirming the field has a managed lifecycle and is released elsewhere during struct cleanup. The result is also NULL-checked at 1681, so this is not a null-deref. The NeverFree finding stems from the analyzer not tracking the free of this struct field outside the slice.

new_sess from ssl_session_dup is either NULL on failure (goto err, nothing to free) or transferred to sc->session at line 3910 after freeing the old session. Ownership is intentionally transferred to the connection's session structure, which is freed during connection cleanup. peer_rpk is freed on the err path. No leak on any feasible path.

new_sess from ssl_session_dup is assigned to s->session at line 4098 after the old session is freed, transferring ownership to the SSL structure. The duplicated session is freed later via the normal SSL session lifecycle, not leaked. On the failure path (==0) it goes to err with nothing allocated. The analyzer flags 'NeverFree' because it does not track ownership transfer into a struct field.
